transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um, well, I guess I'm here because of a little hiccup at work. I work as a cashier, and lately I've just been... getting a bit stuck at the register. 

It's nothing terrible, I promise, I just catch myself doing things that don't really fit the moment. Like, I might start tapping the scanner in a little pattern, or I'll sort of just freeze with my hand hovering over the cash drawer while a customer is waiting. I'm really trying my best to do a good job, but... well, it actually got me written up last week, which is pretty embarrassing to admit. 

I hope it's okay that I came in for that? I just want to get it sorted out so I can be a good employee, if that makes sense.
When you're doing things like tapping the scanner in a pattern, are you aware of what you're doing at the time?

Um, yes, doctor. I think so? I mean, I know I'm doing it. It's not like I black out or anything bad like that, I promise. I just... I realize I'm doing it, but I just sort of get stuck. 

Like I was saying, I'll be tapping the scanner, or I'll see my hand just freezing right over the cash drawer, and I know the customer is standing right there waiting for me. I know what I'm doing doesn't fit the moment at all, but I just can't seem to move on to the next step right away. I really don't mean to cause any delays for anyone, and I feel so terrible that it got me written up. I'm really trying hard to fix it so I can be better at my job. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Do you feel like you have to tap the scanner in a pattern or is it just something you find yourself doing?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I feel like I *have* to do it. It's not like a... a strict rule in my head or an urge or anything bad like that, I promise. I guess I just... I just find myself doing it. 

It's really just a silly little habit that sneaks up on me. I'll just sort of drift into it without thinking, and then I realize, 'Oh, I'm tapping the scanner again.' It's nothing serious, I just need to pay better attention so I don't bother the customers, I think. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Are you having any trouble with your relationships or daily activities outside of work?

Um, well... I guess I should mention, since you asked about how things are going, that the write-up at work... it's actually a formal warning now. I feel just awful about it, I really do. I'm trying so hard to fix it. 

And, well, outside of my shifts... I suppose things have been a little quiet lately? It's nothing terrible, I promise. I just... I guess I’ve sort of stopped keeping up with my friends the way I used to. We used to have these kayaking plans, and I just haven't been going. And I haven't been making my regular family calls, either. 

I'm really going to try to get better about it, though, so I don't let anyone down. I don't want you to think I'm just ignoring everyone or being a bad person, I just... I guess I just haven't been quite as active lately. 

Does that answer your question okay? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you feel anxious or uncomfortable when you try to stop yourself from tapping the scanner in a pattern?

Oh, um... no, doctor. I don't think so. It's not like I get upset or nervous if I have to stop. I promise I don't get agitated or anything bad like that. If I catch myself doing it, or if I notice a customer waiting, I just... I just stop and go back to scanning the groceries. 

It doesn't make me feel panicked or uncomfortable at all. I really just want to do a good job, so I'm happy to stop the second I realize it's happening. I don't want to cause any trouble for anyone. 

Is that what you were asking? I hope I'm explaining things okay for you.
Do you feel like you're avoiding social situations because of your habits or behaviors?

Oh, no, no, it's nothing like that, I promise. I'm not... I'm not hiding away or anything bad. It's really not because of the tapping or any other habits. 

I guess I just... well, I've just been a bit more of a homebody lately, that's all. It's just easier to stay in and rest after a long shift at the store. I definitely don't want you to think I'm avoiding people because I'm embarrassed or acting strange. It's just a little phase of being tired, I think. I'm sure I'll get back to calling my family and going out soon.

I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm not giving you the wrong impression about why I've been quiet.
Do you feel distressed when you think about your habits, like tapping the scanner in a pattern?

Oh, distressed? Um, no. No, I wouldn't use that word at all. I really don't want to make a big fuss out of it, you know? 

It's just a silly little thing I do sometimes, the tapping. It doesn't upset me or make me feel bad. I mean, I know I shouldn't do it, especially at work, and I feel terrible that it caused a problem with my manager... but the actual tapping itself? No, it doesn't bother me or cause me any distress. I'm really trying hard to just be a good employee and keep the line moving. 

I don't want you to worry that I'm, you know, falling apart over it or anything. It's just a little quirk I need to work on. Does that sound alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea about how I'm feeling.
Are your habits, like tapping the scanner, affecting your ability to complete tasks outside of work?

Oh, um... well, I don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart or anything like that. I'm really trying my best to keep everything together. But, um... I guess things have slipped just a little bit lately. 

I actually... well, I got put on a formal warning at work, which I feel just terrible about. I'm going to do much better, I promise you that. And outside of my shifts... I guess I have stopped keeping up with my friends as much. I haven't been going to my kayaking plans, and I kind of stopped making my family calls the way I used to. 

It's not that I can't do these things, I just... I think I've just been a bit overwhelmed and need to recharge quietly. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad person, or a lazy employee. I just want to be completely honest with you so you can help me. Does that answer your question okay?
Do you feel sad or empty when you think about not keeping up with your friends and family like you used to?

Oh, sad? No, no, I wouldn't say sad or empty. I really don't want you to think I'm depressed or, you know, sitting around feeling sorry for myself. I promise I'm not doing that. 

I mean, sure, I miss them a little bit, but it's really just a temporary thing while I get my energy back. I'm totally fine, honestly. I just... I think I just need a little time to myself right now, and they understand that. I'm definitely planning to reach out to everyone again real soon, once I'm feeling a bit more caught up with everything. 

I'm not trying to be a bad friend or a bad son, I really am trying my best. Is it okay that I feel that way? I just don't want you to worry that I'm spiraling or anything like that.
Do you feel like you have to perform these habits, like tapping the scanner, in order to feel right or to prevent something from happening?

Oh, um, to prevent something? No, no, definitely not. I don't want you to think I'm... well, that I have all these irrational fears or anything like that. I'm really trying to keep things very grounded. 

It's really not about stopping something bad from happening, or, you know, feeling like I *have* to do it. It's just... I guess it just became a bit of a habit, you know? Just a rhythm thing with the scanner. I'm certainly not doing it because I feel forced to, or because I'm worried about some terrible consequence if I don't. 

I'm really trying to just be a normal, reliable guy, especially at work. I know I need to stop doing it, and I am trying so hard to just scan things the regular way. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture, and that you don't think I'm getting carried away with strange ideas. Is that a helpful answer?
Do you feel like something bad would happen if you didn't tap the scanner in a pattern?

Oh, um, no. No, I don't think anything bad would happen. I know you asked something similar just a moment ago, and I really don't want you to think I'm holding anything back from you. I promise I'm not. 

I don't have any, like, scary thoughts or worries that something awful is going to happen if I don't do the tapping. It's really just a silly little habit that got out of hand. I know I shouldn't be doing it, and I'm really working on stopping it completely so my boss doesn't have to worry about me anymore. 

I'm just a regular guy who picked up a bad habit at the register, that's all. I really hope I'm explaining this okay. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you know I'm trying my best. Does that make sense?
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and make you want to tap the scanner in a pattern?

Oh, repeating thoughts? No, no, definitely not. I know it probably seems like there must be some big, complicated reason behind it, but I promise there isn't. I really don't want you to think my mind is, you know, stuck on a loop or anything like that. 

My thoughts are totally normal, I swear. It's just... well, like I said, it's just a physical habit with my hands. There's no voice or thought in my head telling me to do it over and over. I'm really trying to be very clear about that, because I don't want to give you the wrong impression about how my mind is working. 

I'm just trying to do my job at the register the best I can, and I know the tapping is a distraction. I'm going to stop, I really am. I hope you believe me when I say that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the answers you need and that I'm not making things sound worse than they are. Am I doing okay explaining this?
Do you feel like tapping the scanner is something you do on impulse, without thinking about it beforehand?

Well, um, impulse? I guess, maybe a little bit? I mean, I don't plan it out or anything. It's just... well, honestly, I came in because these things at the register, they just sort of happen. Like, I get stuck doing things that don't really fit what I'm supposed to be doing right then. 

Like the tapping, like we talked about, or... sometimes I just sort of freeze up, you know? Like, I'll have my hand right over the open cash drawer, and the customer is just standing there waiting for their change, and I just... stop. It's really embarrassing, and I don't want you to think I'm doing it on purpose to be difficult or anything. 

It actually got me written up last week, which is why I'm here. I really want to fix it so I can just be a good employee again. I know it sounds a little odd, getting stuck like that, but I'm really trying my best to just be normal at work. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound too strange... I just want to be honest with you so you can tell I'm trying to do the right thing.
Do you feel like your habits at work are causing you significant stress or anxiety outside of your job?

Oh, stress outside of work? No, no, definitely not. Um, when I clock out, I really try to just leave it all there, you know? I don't want you to think I'm, like, falling apart at home or anything. I'm really doing just fine once my shift is over. 

I just go back to my place, maybe watch a little TV, have dinner... just normal, everyday stuff. I really don't want to make a big fuss or sound like I'm complaining, because I'm honestly not sitting around worrying when I'm off the clock. I'm managing everything just fine on my own time. 

I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I just want to reassure you that I'm keeping it together and trying to be as normal as possible. I want to be a good patient for you and not make things seem worse than they are. Did I explain that okay? I really don't want you to have to worry about me too much.
Do you feel like you are doing these habits because you feel compelled to, even if you don't want to?

Compelled? Um... no, no, I wouldn't say compelled. That sounds a bit... well, like I have absolutely no control over myself, and I promise that's not the case at all. I really don't want you to think I'm completely unmanageable or anything like that. 

It's not like I feel forced to do it... it's really just a bad habit that slips out before I catch myself. But I can stop, I really can. I'm working very hard on catching it early so I can be better at the register. I don't want to be a problem employee, you know? 

I hope that's okay to say? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea, because I don't want to make it sound like some big, scary urge that I can't fight. I'm honestly trying my best to cooperate and fix this. Does that answer your question all right?
Do you feel like you're doing these habits without fully thinking them through beforehand?

Without thinking? Um... well, no, I don't think so. I really don't want you to get the impression that I'm just... acting mindlessly or checked out at work. I'm actually trying very hard to pay attention to everything, especially since my manager talked to me. 

So I wouldn't say I do them without thinking at all. I mean, I'm right there, focusing on the customer and the cash drawer. I just... well, I guess I'm not entirely sure how to explain it, but I promise I'm not just spacing out and doing things without any thought. I really do try to be a good, attentive employee. 

Is that... does that answer what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you know I'm taking this seriously.
Do you feel like your habits at the register are causing you a lot of distress?

Distress? Oh, um... no, definitely not distress. That sounds so severe, and I really don't want you to think I'm, you know, falling apart at the register or getting upset in front of the customers. I promise I'm keeping a good attitude about everything. 

I mean, sure, it's a little frustrating that my manager had to talk to me about it, but it doesn't upset me deeply or anything like that. I can handle it. I just... I want to be a good employee, and I'm trying to just take it all in stride. 

I hope it's okay that I don't feel distressed by it? I just really want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture, so you know I'm staying positive and not letting things get to me. Does that sound alright to you? I really want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Do you often find yourself acting on impulse in other areas of your life, not just at work?

Impulse? Oh, no... no, I wouldn't say I'm an impulsive person. That sounds a bit reckless, doesn't it? Like I'm just doing things wildly without caring about the consequences, and I promise I'm very careful. I really try to be responsible and think things through, at home and everywhere else.

I don't just go out and buy things on a whim or, you know, make big decisions without planning. I like to keep things steady and predictable. I really don't want you to think I'm out of control in my personal life, because I'm honestly very sensible. 

I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to make sure you know I'm a reliable person, not someone who just acts on impulse all the time. Is that okay to say?
Do you think your habits at the register are more like something you do without thinking, or something you feel like you need to do?

Well, I wouldn't say I do them without thinking, because I really am trying to pay attention. But... well, I suppose it's more like I just get a little... caught up in things. 

Like, sometimes I'll be ringing someone up, and I might just tap the scanner a few times in a certain way. Or... or I might pause for a second, you know, just holding my hand over the cash drawer before I give the change. It's not that I feel forced to do it, it just sort of happens, and then the customer is just standing there waiting. 

I know it sounds a little silly, and I really don't want you to think I'm doing it on purpose to be difficult. It's just a little quirk, really. But my manager did notice, and... well, she actually wrote me up for it last week. That's actually why I came in to see you. I just want to figure out how to stop doing those little things so I can be the best cashier possible. 

I hope it's okay that I'm telling you this? I just want to be honest so you can help me, but I really don't want you to think I'm a bad worker. Does that make sense?
Do you feel like you're doing these habits because you can't resist doing them, even if you know you shouldn't?

Oh, no... I wouldn't use the word "resist." That makes it sound like... like I have some kind of terrible urge I'm fighting, and I really don't want you to think I'm out of control like that. 

It's not like I'm sitting there feeling forced to do it. I promise I'm not deliberately doing things I know I shouldn't. I always try to follow my manager's instructions to the letter. It's just... I don't know, sometimes my hands just sort of do the tapping or the pausing before I fully realize it's happening. 

But it's definitely not because I *have* to do it. If I catch myself, I can stop right away. I'm very capable of stopping, I just need to pay better attention to my movements, that's all. 

I hope that's the right way to explain it? I just really want you to know I'm trying hard to be compliant and fix this, and I'm not just ignoring the rules. Does that answer your question okay?
